mock_data.title: Who Wants a Predictable Life?
mock_data.passage:
A New Scientist games column by Jacob Aron on roguelike games as storytelling machines, and how the balance between order and randomness determines whether they truly work.

When Apple launched the iPod Shuffle, people complained that its shuffling function didn't work as advertised – songs by the same artist seemed to be clustering, so one David Bowie track, say, would swiftly be followed by another.

In fact, this kind of clustering is exactly what we would expect. A random algorithm makes no effort to "remember" what has come before, so it makes for an unsatisfying listening experience. In the end, Apple tweaked its software to avoid repetition. "We're making it less random to make it feel more random," said the CEO at the time, Steve Jobs.

I was reminded of this playing Rad, a game set in a 1980s-tinged future following not one, but two apocalypses. As you explore a nuclear wasteland and vanquish enemies, your character randomly mutates to gain new abilities, such as an arm that shoots fire or a snake head that spits poison.

Rad is a roguelike, a genre named after the 1980 game Rogue, which sees players delve into a dungeon full of monsters and magic items (itself inspired by the classic Dungeons & Dragons). Rogue uses text characters to represent everything in the world, for example, the @ symbol is the player. Meanwhile, the dungeon is generated by an algorithm each time you start up, giving it the potential for huge variety.

I like to think of roguelikes as storytelling machines – ideally, your experience will be completely different from someone else's, making it fun to swap anecdotes with friends. That said, like the altered version of the iPod Shuffle, roguelikes aren't truly random – if they were, you'd end up with a game that was impossible to complete. In other words, a dash of order is key to making randomness enjoyable.

Unfortunately, Rad hasn't quite got the balance right. Surprise and discovery are a huge part of the roguelike genre, but with Rad, I found myself acquiring the same mutations again and again. Each time I died and started a new game, I had less of an urge to continue playing, as it felt like I wasn't seeing anything novel, which doesn't make for a great story.

Other roguelikes are well worth checking out, however. Spelunky, the king of modern roguelikes, is a near-perfect balance of order and chaos. The levels are never the same, but everything within the game is utterly predictable, allowing you to set up chains of actions such as throwing a bomb to blast a stone into the air, triggering a trap to kill a snake. You can't help but laugh as you play.

For my taste, though, Spelunky is still a bit unforgiving as you start from scratch every time. I prefer Rogue Legacy, which sees you play as a member of a long-running dynasty, each with their own quirks such as short-sightedness or vertigo. When you die, you get to keep certain items and upgrades from the previous run, allowing you to progress further into the game's randomly generated castle. This persistence isn't completely true to the roots of the roguelike genre, but it strikes the right balance for me.

Finally, some roguelikes abandon the dungeon trapping, but retain the randomness to generate unique experiences. If you are a Star Trek fan, check out FTL: Faster Than Light, which has you command a spacecraft and crew. Hopping between star systems, you can live out your Captain Picard fantasies, managing power levels, or depressurising the ship to put out fires. Just don't jettison the crew.
mock_data.passageB1:
Have you ever thought about what makes a game fun? A writer named Jacob Aron wrote about a type of game called “roguelike” games. He said these games are like storytelling machines. The way these games mix order and chance is important for making them good.

A long time ago, Apple made a music player called the iPod Shuffle. People said that the shuffle feature didn't work well. It seemed like songs by the same singer would play one after another.

This is actually what you would expect if something is truly random. A random system doesn't “remember” what it played before. So, listening to music this way wasn't very enjoyable. Apple changed the software to stop songs from repeating too quickly. The boss of Apple, Steve Jobs, said they made it “less random to make it feel more random.”

This idea reminded me of a game called Rad. The game is set in the future after bad things have happened twice. When you play, you explore a nuclear wasteland and fight enemies. Your character changes randomly and gets new abilities. For example, you might get an arm that shoots fire or a snake head that spits poison.

Rad is a roguelike game. This kind of game is named after a game from the 1980s called Rogue. In Rogue, players go into a dungeon filled with monsters and magic items. The game was inspired by the game Dungeons & Dragons. Rogue uses letters and symbols to show everything in the game. For example, the @ symbol is the player. Each time you start the game, the dungeon is created by a computer program, so it's always different.

Roguelike games can create unique experiences. Ideally, your game will be different from everyone else's. This makes it fun to talk about the game with friends. But, like the iPod Shuffle, roguelike games aren't completely random. If they were, the game would be too hard to finish. A little bit of order is needed to make the randomness fun.

Rad doesn't quite get this balance right. Surprise and finding new things are important in roguelike games. But in Rad, I kept getting the same changes again and again. Each time I died and started a new game, I didn't want to play anymore. It felt like I wasn't seeing anything new, which made the story boring.

However, there are other roguelike games that are worth playing. Spelunky is one of the best modern roguelike games. It has a good balance of order and chaos. The levels are always different, but everything in the game behaves in a way that you can guess. This lets you do things like throw a bomb to move a stone, which sets off a trap to kill a snake. It's hard not to laugh when you play.

For me, Spelunky is a little too hard because you have to start over every time you die. I like Rogue Legacy better. In this game, you play as members of a family, and each family member has their own quirks, like bad eyesight or feeling dizzy. When you die, you get to keep some things from the last game. This helps you go further into the castle that changes each time you play. This isn't exactly how roguelike games started, but it's a good balance for me.

Finally, some roguelike games don't have dungeons, but they still use randomness to make unique experiences. If you like Star Trek, you should try FTL: Faster Than Light. In this game, you command a spaceship and crew. You travel between star systems and can pretend to be Captain Picard. You can control power levels or let air out of the ship to put out fires. Just don't throw the crew out of the ship!

These games show how mixing order and randomness can make compelling experiences. The best ones find the right balance to keep you playing and make each game feel like a new adventure. Whether it's exploring a nuclear wasteland or commanding a spaceship, roguelike games offer something for everyone who enjoys a bit of the unexpected.

So, next time you're looking for a game, think about whether you want something predictable or something that will surprise you. Roguelike games might just be the perfect choice if you're looking for a unique and unforgettable experience. Just remember, the key is finding that sweet spot where order and chaos come together to create something truly special. And who knows, you might just find yourself immersed in a world where anything can happen, and every playthrough is a new story waiting to be told.

Ultimately, the appeal of roguelike games lies in their ability to offer a fresh and engaging experience every time you play. It's about embracing the unforeseen, adapting to new challenges, and creating your own unique narrative within the game's framework. So, if you're ready to step outside your comfort zone and embark on a gaming journey filled with surprises, roguelike games might just be the perfect escape you've been searching for.
mock_data.passageB2:
Have you ever wondered why a perfectly predictable life might not be as appealing as it sounds? A recent article in New Scientist, written by Jacob Aron, looks at “roguelike” video games and how they create stories. These games rely on a delicate balance between order and randomness to be truly successful.

Think back to when Apple first released the iPod Shuffle. Many users complained that the shuffle function wasn't working properly. They noticed that songs by the same artist would often play one after another – a series of David Bowie tracks, for example. This seemed strange, as they expected a truly random selection.

However, this “clustering” effect is actually what you’d expect from a truly random algorithm. A random system doesn't try to “remember” what it has already played. This can lead to a less than ideal listening experience. Apple eventually adjusted the software to reduce repetition. As Steve Jobs, the CEO at the time, put it, “We’re making it less random to make it feel more random.” This counterintuitive approach highlights how true randomness can sometimes be unsatisfying.

This idea came to mind while playing Rad, a game set in a future that feels like the 1980s after not one, but two, apocalypses. As you explore a nuclear wasteland and defeat enemies, your character undergoes random mutations. These mutations give you new abilities, such as an arm that shoots fire or a snake head that spits poison. The game's premise is compelling, but the execution needs work.

Rad is a roguelike game, named after the 1980 game Rogue. In Rogue, players explore a dungeon filled with monsters and magical items. This was itself inspired by the classic game Dungeons & Dragons. Rogue used text characters to represent everything in the game world. For instance, the @ symbol represented the player. The dungeon was generated by an algorithm each time you started a new game, offering a huge amount of potential variety. Roguelikes have become a popular genre of video game and often boast a high level of replayability.

I like to think of roguelikes as storytelling machines. Ideally, each player's experience should be unique. This makes it fun to share stories with friends. However, like the adjusted iPod Shuffle, roguelikes aren't truly random. If they were, the game would be impossible to complete. In other words, a bit of order is essential to making the randomness enjoyable. It's a question of finding the optimal level of unpredictability.

Unfortunately, Rad doesn't quite get this balance right. Surprise and discovery are crucial to the roguelike genre. But in Rad, I kept getting the same mutations over and over again. Each time I died and started a new game, I felt less motivated to keep playing. It felt like I wasn't seeing anything new, which doesn't make for a very interesting story. The game becomes repetitive and loses its initial appeal.

However, there are other roguelikes that are worth checking out. Spelunky, often considered the benchmark of modern roguelikes, achieves a near-perfect balance of order and chaos. The levels are always different, but the rules of the game are completely predictable. This allows you to create complex chains of actions, like throwing a bomb to blast a stone into the air, which triggers a trap that kills a snake. It's hard not to laugh while playing.

Personally, I find Spelunky a bit too difficult because you start from scratch every time you die. I prefer Rogue Legacy, where you play as a member of a family dynasty, each with unique traits like nearsightedness or vertigo. When you die, you get to keep certain items and upgrades from the previous run. This allows you to progress further into the game's randomly generated castle. This element of persistence isn't strictly true to the original roguelike concept, but it works well for me. It offers a good balance between challenge and reward.

Finally, some roguelikes move away from the dungeon setting but keep the randomness to create unique experiences. If you're a Star Trek fan, check out FTL: Faster Than Light. In this game, you command a spacecraft and its crew. As you travel between star systems, you can live out your Captain Picard fantasies. You can manage power levels or depressurize the ship to put out fires. Just try not to eject any crew members! This shows how the roguelike formula can be adapted to different genres and settings, offering fresh and exciting gameplay.
mock_data.passageC1:
The seemingly innocuous feature of shuffling music, as exemplified by the early iPod Shuffle, unexpectedly reveals a deeper truth about our perception of randomness. Initial user feedback highlighted a peculiar clustering effect – tracks by the same artist playing in close succession – which, counterintuitively, stemmed from the algorithm's very adherence to pure randomness. This led Apple to fine-tune its software, paradoxically making it 'less random' to engender a more satisfying, seemingly random listening experience. This anecdote serves as a useful analogue for understanding the delicate balance required in the design of roguelike video games.

Jacob Aron, in his New Scientist games column, posits that roguelikes function as storytelling machines, their efficacy hinging on the precise calibration between order and randomness. Named after the seminal 1980 game Rogue, the genre throws players into procedurally generated dungeons teeming with monsters and magical artifacts. Each playthrough promises a unique experience, theoretically allowing for endlessly shareable and diverse player narratives. However, much like Apple's initial shuffling algorithm, a purely random roguelike would likely prove frustratingly unplayable. A modicum of predictability, therefore, is indispensable to maintaining player engagement and ensuring a semblance of progress.

Rad, a game set in a retro-futuristic, post-apocalyptic landscape, unfortunately, fails to strike this balance effectively. While its premise – exploring a nuclear wasteland and battling enemies whilst acquiring random mutations – holds promise, the actual gameplay experience leaves something to be desired. The repetitive nature of the mutations, the feeling of constantly encountering the same abilities upon each death and subsequent restart, diminishes the sense of discovery that is paramount to the roguelike experience. This lack of novelty ultimately stifles the emergent narrative, rendering each playthrough less compelling than the last.

By contrast, titles like Spelunky exemplify the successful integration of order and chaos. Its levels are perpetually different, yet the underlying mechanics remain consistent and predictable. This allows players to orchestrate complex chains of actions, such as strategically detonating bombs to trigger traps, leading to emergent and often hilarious outcomes. The predictability of the game's physics, coupled with the unpredictability of the level design, creates a compelling and rewarding gameplay loop. However, Spelunky's unforgiving nature – the complete loss of progress upon death – may prove off-putting to some players.

For those seeking a more forgiving experience, Rogue Legacy offers an intriguing twist on the genre. By introducing a persistent element – a generational dynasty of characters, each with unique traits and abilities – the game mitigates the frustration of starting from scratch after each death. While this deviation from the traditional roguelike formula might raise eyebrows among purists, it arguably provides a more accessible and ultimately more enjoyable experience. The ability to retain certain items and upgrades between runs allows players to gradually progress further into the randomly generated castle, fostering a sense of accomplishment that is often lacking in more traditional roguelikes.

Beyond the confines of dungeon crawlers, the roguelike ethos extends to other genres. FTL: Faster Than Light, a space exploration and combat simulator, retains the core element of randomness to generate unique and compelling narratives. As the captain of a spacecraft, players must navigate a hostile galaxy, managing resources, engaging in tactical combat, and making difficult decisions that can have far-reaching consequences. The unpredictable nature of encounters, coupled with the permanent death of crew members, ensures that each playthrough is a unique and often heart-wrenching experience. Ultimately, the enduring appeal of roguelikes lies in their ability to conjure emergent narratives through the carefully calibrated interplay of order and chaos, offering players a truly unique and unpredictable gaming experience.

mock_data.translation:
Jeykob Aron tomonidan yozilgan New Scientist o'yinlar ustuni — roguelike o'yinlar hikoya quradigan mashinalar sifatida va tartib bilan tasodifiylik orasidagi muvozanat ularning ishlashini qanday belgilashi haqida.

Apple iPod Shuffle-ni ishga chiqqanda, odamlar uning aralashtirish funksiyasi reklama qilinganidek ishlamasligidan shikoyat qilishdi — bir xil san'atkorning qo'shiqlari to'planib qolayotganday tuyulardi, shuning uchun bitta David Bowie treki, masalan, tezda boshqa biri bilan davom etardi.

Aslida, bunday to'planish aynan biz kutgan narsa. Tasodifiy algoritm oldingi narsalarni "eslab qolish"ga hech qanday harakat qilmaydi, shuning uchun bu qoniqarsiz tinglash tajribasiga olib keladi. Oxir-oqibat, Apple takroriylikdan qochish uchun dasturiy ta'minotini o'zgartirdi. "Biz uni tasodifiy his qildirish uchun kamroq tasodifiy qilmoqdamiz," dedi o'sha paytdagi bosh direktor Stiv Jobs.

Menga bu Rad o'yinini o'ynayotganda esga tushdi — 1980-yillar uslubidagi kelajakda joylashgan o'yin, bitta emas, balki ikkita apokalipsisdan keyin. Siz yadroviy xarobalarni o'rganib, dushmanlarni mag'lub qilganingizda, sizning qahramon tasodifiy ravishda yangi qobiliyatlarga ega bo'lish uchun o'zgaradi, masalan, olov otadigan qo'l yoki zahar tupuradigan ilon boshi.

Rad — roguelike, 1980-yilgi Rogue o'yini nomi bilan atalgan janr bo'lib, o'yinchilarni yirtqich hayvonlar va sehrli buyumlar bilan to'la zindonga kirishga undaydi (o'zi klassik Dungeons & Dragons dan ilhomlangan). Rogue dunyodagi hamma narsani ifodalash uchun matnli belgilardan foydalanadi, masalan, @ belgisi o'yinchi. Shu bilan birga, zindon har safar o'yinni boshlaganingizda algoritm tomonidan yaratiladi, bu katta xilma-xillik potentsialini beradi.

Men roguelike-larni hikoya quradigan mashinalar deb o'ylashni yaxshi ko'raman — ideal holda, sizning tajribangiz boshqa birovnikidan butunlay farq qiladi, bu do'stlar bilan latifalar almashishni qiziqarli qiladi. Shunga qaramay, iPod Shuffle-ning o'zgartirilgan versiyasiga o'xshab, roguelike-lar haqiqatan ham tasodifiy emas — agar shunday bo'lganda, siz tugatish mumkin bo'lmagan o'yin bilan tugardingiz. Boshqacha qilib aytganda, bir oz tartib tasodifiylikni yoqimli qilishning kalitidir.

Afsuski, Rad muvozanatni to'g'ri topa olmadi. Kutilmaganlik va kashfiyot roguelike janrining katta qismi, lekin Rad bilan men bir xil mutatsiyalarni qayta-qayta olayotganimni payqadim. Har safar o'lganimda va yangi o'yinni boshlaganimda, o'yinni davom ettirishga kamroq istak bor edi, chunki men yangi hech narsa ko'rmayotgandek his qilardim, bu ajoyib hikoya yaratmaydi.

Biroq boshqa roguelike-lar tekshirishga arziydi. Spelunky, zamonaviy roguelike-larning shohi, tartib va tartibsizlikning deyarli mukammal muvozanati. Darajalar hech qachon bir xil bo'lmaydi, lekin o'yindagi hamma narsa butunlay bashorat qilinadigan, bu sizga harakatlar zanjirini o'rnatishga imkon beradi, masalan, toshni havoga uchirish uchun bomba tashlash, ilonni o'ldirish uchun tuzoqni ishga tushirish. Siz o'ynayotganingizda kulmasdan tura olmaysiz.

Lekin mening didim uchun Spelunky hali ham biroz shafqatsiz, chunki siz har safar noldan boshlaysiz. Men Rogue Legacyni afzal ko'raman, unda siz uzoq davom etgan sulolaning a'zosi sifatida o'ynaysiz, har birining o'ziga xos xususiyatlari bor, masalan, yaqindan ko'ra olmaslik yoki bosh aylanishi. O'lganingizda, oldingi yurishdan ma'lum buyumlar va yangilanishlarni saqlab qolasiz, bu sizga o'yinning tasodifiy yaratilgan qal'asiga chuqurroq kirishga imkon beradi. Bu barqarorlik roguelike janrining ildizlariga to'liq mos kelmaydi, lekin men uchun to'g'ri muvozanatni topadi.

Nihoyat, ba'zi roguelike-lar zindon tuzoqlarini tark etadi, lekin noyob tajribalar yaratish uchun tasodifiylikni saqlab qoladi. Agar siz Star Trek muxlisi bo'lsangiz, FTL: Faster Than Lightni ko'ring, u sizga kosmik kema va ekipajni boshqarish imkonini beradi. Yulduz tizimlari o'rtasida sakrab, siz Kapitan Pikard fantasiyalaringizni amalga oshirishingiz, quvvat darajalarini boshqarishingiz yoki yong'inlarni o'chirish uchun kemani bosimdan bo'shatishingiz mumkin. Faqat ekipajni tashlab yubormang.

Hech qachon o‘yinni nima qiziqarli qilishi haqida o‘ylab ko‘rganmisiz? Jacob Aron ismli yozuvchi “roguelike” o‘yinlari deb nomlanuvchi o‘yin turi haqida yozgan. Uning aytishicha, bu o‘yinlar xuddi hikoya yaratish mashinalariga o‘xshaydi. Ushbu o‘yinlarning tartib va tasodifni aralashtirish usuli ularni yaxshi qiladi.

Qadim zamonlarda Apple iPod Shuffle deb nomlangan musiqa pleerini yaratgan. Odamlar shuffle funksiyasi yaxshi ishlamayapti, deyishgan. Xuddi shu qo‘shiqchining qo‘shiqlari birin-ketin yangragandek tuyulgan.

Aslida, bu narsa chindan ham tasodifiy bo‘lsa, siz kutishingiz mumkin bo‘lgan narsadir. Tasodifiy tizim avval nima ijro etganini "eslamaydi". Shunday qilib, bu tarzda musiqa tinglash unchalik yoqimli emas edi. Apple dasturiy ta'minotni qo‘shiqlar juda tez takrorlanishini to‘xtatish uchun o‘zgartirdi. Apple kompaniyasining rahbari Stiv Jobs ularni "tasodifiyroq his qilish uchun kamroq tasodifiy" qilishganini aytdi.

Bu g‘oya menga Rad deb nomlangan o‘yinni eslatdi. O‘yin kelajakda yomon voqealar ikki marta sodir bo‘lganidan keyin bo‘lib o‘tadi. O‘ynayotganingizda, siz yadroviy cho‘lni o‘rganasiz va dushmanlarga qarshi kurashasiz. Sizning personajingiz tasodifiy ravishda o‘zgaradi va yangi qobiliyatlarga ega bo‘ladi. Misol uchun, sizda olov otadigan qo‘l yoki zaharni tupuradigan ilon boshi paydo bo‘lishi mumkin.

Rad - bu roguelike o'yin. Ushbu turdagi o'yin 1980-yillardagi Rogue o'yinidan keyin nomlangan. Rogue-da o'yinchilar maxluqlar va sehrli narsalarga to'la zindonga kirishadi. O'yin Dungeons & Dragons o'yinidan ilhomlangan. Rogue o'yindagi hamma narsani ko'rsatish uchun harflar va belgilardan foydalanadi. Masalan, @ belgisi o'yinchi hisoblanadi. Har safar o'yinni boshlaganingizda, zindon kompyuter dasturi tomonidan yaratiladi, shuning uchun u har doim boshqacha bo'ladi.

Roguelike o'yinlari noyob tajribalarni yaratishi mumkin. Ideal holda, sizning o'yiningiz boshqalarnikidan farq qiladi. Bu do'stlaringiz bilan o'yin haqida gaplashishni qiziqarli qiladi. Ammo, iPod Shuffle singari, roguelike o'yinlari ham butunlay tasodifiy emas. Agar shunday bo'lganda, o'yinni tugatish juda qiyin bo'lar edi. Tasodifiylikni qiziqarli qilish uchun bir oz tartib kerak.

Rad bu muvozanatni to‘g‘ri yo‘lga qo‘ymaydi. Kutilmagan hodisa va yangi narsalarni topish roguelike o'yinlarida muhimdir. Ammo Rad-da men doim bir xil o'zgarishlarni qayta-qayta olardim. Har safar o'lib, yangi o'yinni boshlaganimda, endi o'ynashni xohlamadim. Go'yo men hech qanday yangi narsa ko'rmayotgandek tuyuldi, bu hikoyani zerikarli qildi.

Biroq, o'ynashga arziydigan boshqa roguelike o'yinlari ham bor. Spelunky - eng yaxshi zamonaviy roguelike o'yinlaridan biri. Unda tartib va xaosning yaxshi muvozanati bor. Darajalar har doim boshqacha, ammo o'yindagi hamma narsa siz taxmin qila oladigan tarzda o'zini tutadi. Bu sizga toshni siljitish uchun bomba uloqtirish, bu tuzoqni ishga tushirib, ilonni o'ldirish kabi ishlarni bajarishga imkon beradi. O'ynaganingizda kulmaslik qiyin.

Men uchun Spelunky biroz qiyin, chunki har safar o'lganingizda qaytadan boshlashingiz kerak. Menga Rogue Legacy ko'proq yoqadi. Ushbu o'yinda siz oila a'zolari sifatida o'ynaysiz va har bir oila a'zosining o'z g'alati xususiyatlari bor, masalan, ko'zning yomonligi yoki bosh aylanishi. O'lganingizda, oxirgi o'yindan ba'zi narsalarni saqlab qolishingiz mumkin. Bu har safar o'zgarib turadigan qasrga chuqurroq kirishga yordam beradi. Bu roguelike o'yinlari qanday boshlanganiga aniq mos kelmaydi, lekin bu men uchun yaxshi muvozanat.

Nihoyat, ba'zi roguelike o'yinlarida zindonlar yo'q, lekin ular hali ham noyob tajribalar yaratish uchun tasodifiylikdan foydalanadilar. Agar sizga Star Trek yoqsa, FTL: Faster Than Light-ni sinab ko'rishingiz kerak. Ushbu o'yinda siz kosmik kemaga va ekipajga qo'mondonlik qilasiz. Siz yulduz tizimlari o'rtasida sayohat qilasiz va kapitan Pikarddek bo'lishingiz mumkin. Siz quvvat darajalarini boshqarishingiz yoki yong'inni o'chirish uchun kemadan havoni chiqarib yuborishingiz mumkin. Faqat ekipajni kemadan uloqtirmang!

Ushbu o'yinlar tartib va tasodifiylikni aralashtirish qanday qilib qiziqarli tajribalarni yaratishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi. Eng yaxshilari sizni o'ynashga undash va har bir o'yinni yangi sarguzasht kabi his qilish uchun to'g'ri muvozanatni topadi. Yadroviy cho'lni o'rganish yoki kosmik kemaga qo'mondonlik qilish bo'ladimi, roguelike o'yinlari bir oz kutilmagan narsalardan zavqlanadigan har bir kishi uchun nimadir taklif qiladi.

Shunday qilib, keyingi safar o'yin qidirayotganingizda, siz bashorat qilinadigan narsani xohlaysizmi yoki sizni hayratda qoldiradigan narsani xohlaysizmi, deb o'ylab ko'ring. Agar siz noyob va unutilmas tajriba qidirayotgan bo'lsangiz, roguelike o'yinlari ajoyib tanlov bo'lishi mumkin. Shuni esda tutingki, eng muhimi, tartib va xaos birgalikda chindan ham maxsus narsani yaratadigan o'sha ajoyib nuqtani topishdir. Va kim biladi, siz o'zingizni hamma narsa bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan dunyoga sho'ng'ib ketgan holda topishingiz mumkin va har bir o'yin yangi hikoya aytilishini kutmoqda.

Oxir oqibat, roguelike o'yinlarining jozibasi har safar o'ynaganingizda yangi va qiziqarli tajriba taklif qilish qobiliyatida yotadi. Bu kutilmagan narsani qabul qilish, yangi qiyinchiliklarga moslashish va o'yin doirasida o'z noyob hikoyangizni yaratish haqida. Shunday qilib, agar siz o'z qulaylik hududingizdan chiqishga va kutilmagan hodisalarga to'la o'yin sayohatiga kirishishga tayyor bo'lsangiz, roguelike o'yinlari siz qidirayotgan mukammal qochish bo'lishi mumkin.

Musiqani tasodifiy tartibda chalish xususiyati, xuddi dastlabki iPod Shuffle misolida ko'rinib turgandek, tasodif haqidagi tushunchamizning chuqurroq haqiqatini kutilmaganda ochib beradi. Bu Apple kompaniyasini o'z dasturini nozik sozlashga olib keldi, paradoksal ravishda uni "kamroq tasodifiy" qilib, yanada qoniqarli, go'yoki tasodifiy tinglash tajribasini yaratdi. Bu voqea roguelike video o'yinlar dizaynida talab etiladigan nozik muvozanatni tushunish uchun foydali analogiya bo'lib xizmat qiladi.

Jacob Aron, o'zining New Scientist gazetasidagi o'yinlar ruknida, roguelikelar hikoya yaratish mashinalari sifatida ishlaydi, ularning samaradorligi tartib va tasodifiylik o'rtasidagi aniq kalibrlashga bog'liq, deb ta'kidlaydi. 1980-yillardagi Rogue o'yinidan nomlangan janr o'yinchilarni maxluqlar va sehrli artefaktlarga to'la procedural tarzda yaratilgan zindonlarga tashlaydi. Har bir o'yin noyob tajribani va'da qiladi, nazariy jihatdan cheksiz baham ko'rish mumkin bo'lgan va xilma-xil o'yinchi hikoyalarini yaratishga imkon beradi. Biroq, Apple kompaniyasining dastlabki tartibda chalish algoritmi singari, sof tasodifiy roguelike o'yin o'ynash uchun juda asabiy bo'lishi mumkin. Shuning uchun, o'yinchi ishtirokini saqlab qolish va taraqqiyotga o'xshashlikni ta'minlash uchun bir oz bashorat qilish muhim.

Retro-futuristik, post-apokaliptik landshaftda joylashgan Rad o'yini, afsuski, bu muvozanatni saqlashda yetarlicha muvaffaqiyat qozonmaydi. Uning asosiy g'oyasi – yadroviy cho'lni o'rganish va dushmanlarga qarshi kurashish, shu bilan birga tasodifiy mutatsiyalarni olish – umid baxsh etsa-da, haqiqiy o'yin tajribasi yaxshiroq bo'lishini istaydi. Mutatsiyalarning takroriyligi, har bir o'lim va keyingi qayta boshlashda bir xil qobiliyatlarga duch kelish hissi, roguelike tajribasi uchun muhim bo'lgan kashfiyot tuyg'usini kamaytiradi. Yangilikning yetishmasligi pirovardida rivojlanayotgan hikoyani bo'g'ib qo'yadi va har bir o'yinni avvalgisidan kamroq qiziqarli qiladi.

Aksincha, Spelunky kabi nomlar tartib va xaosning muvaffaqiyatli integratsiyasini namoyish etadi. Uning darajalari doimiy ravishda farq qiladi, ammo asosiy mexanika izchil va bashorat qilinadigan bo'lib qoladi. Bu o'yinchilarga murakkab harakatlar zanjirini boshqarishga imkon beradi, masalan, tuzoqlarni ishga tushirish uchun bombalarni strategik portlatish, bu rivojlanayotgan va ko'pincha kulgili natijalarga olib keladi. O'yin fizikasining bashorat qilinishi, daraja dizaynining oldindan aytib bo'lmasligi bilan birgalikda, qiziqarli va foydali o'yin aylanishini yaratadi. Biroq, Spelunkyning shafqatsiz tabiati – o'limdan keyin taraqqiyotning to'liq yo'qolishi – ba'zi o'yinchilar uchun yoqimsiz bo'lishi mumkin.

Yengilroq tajriba izlayotganlar uchun Rogue Legacy janrga qiziqarli burilishni taklif etadi. Doimiy elementni – har biri o'ziga xos xususiyatlar va qobiliyatlariga ega bo'lgan avlodlar sulolasini kiritish orqali o'yin har bir o'limdan keyin noldan boshlashning asabiyligini kamaytiradi. Yugurishlar orasida ma'lum narsalar va yaxshilanishlarni saqlab qolish qobiliyati o'yinchilarga tasodifiy yaratilgan qasrga asta-sekin kirishga imkon beradi va ko'proq an'anaviy roguelikelarda ko'pincha etishmaydigan yutuq tuyg'usini uyg'otadi.

Zindonlarni bosib o'tish doirasidan tashqari, roguelike ruh boshqa janrlarga ham tarqaladi. FTL: Faster Than Light, kosmik tadqiqot va jang simulyatori, noyob va qiziqarli hikoyalarni yaratish uchun tasodifiylikning asosiy elementini saqlab qoladi. Kosmik kemaning sardori sifatida o'yinchilar dushman galaktikasida harakatlanishlari, resurslarni boshqarishlari, taktik janglarda qatnashishlari va uzoq muddatli oqibatlarga olib keladigan qiyin qarorlar qabul qilishlari kerak. Uchrashuvlarning oldindan aytib bo'lmasligi, ekipaj a'zolarining doimiy o'limi bilan birgalikda, har bir o'yin noyob va ko'pincha yurakni ezuvchi tajriba bo'lishini ta'minlaydi. Oxir oqibat, roguelikelarning doimiy jozibasi tartib va xaosning ehtiyotkorlik bilan kalibrlangan o'zaro ta'siri orqali rivojlanayotgan hikoyalarni yaratish qobiliyatida yotadi va o'yinchilarga haqiqatan ham noyob va oldindan aytib bo'lmaydigan o'yin tajribasini taklif qiladi.
